newsitem.title: JAPAN: UPS, Nippon Cargo in air cargo tie-up.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Nippon Cargo in air cargo tie-up.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc (UPS) and Nippon Cargo Airlines (NCA) said on Friday they had agreed on a long-term business tie-up, including sharing freighter flights.
The companies said they will implement an interline arrangement on October 30 under which one airline would entrust cargo to the other.
The two companies also plan a code-share service beginning from mid-1997, subject to government approvals, and have begun discussions on further expanding business ties, they said.
The tie-up follows a successful conclusion to a U.S.-Japan all-cargo aviation agreement in April, the statement said.
Under that agreement, UPS was awarded rights to operate 12 additional weekly flights from the United States to Osaka and beyond Osaka to two locations in Asia.
NCA was also granted approval to increase flight frequencies to the U.S. by 30 roundtrips per week, and the right to designate three new U.S. points for services.
Earlier this year, the Japanese all-cargo air carrier also hammered out an agreement with another U.S. air carrier on broad cooperation.

In June, Nippon Cargo agreed with Northwest Airlines Inc, a unit of Northwest Corp agreed on a wide range of cooperative marketing and operational programmes, including a cargo service from Osaka to Chicago.
Under the agreement, the two companies granted each other access to their Osaka-Chicago freighter flights. As a result, they now each offer four weekly services.
